messages.author: c40e5eaac12f63d6
messages.subject: Installing R packages on nodes
parts:
G'day 

I am setting up an RHadoop cluster for teaching mapreduce to undergrads. We will use RStudio as the interface. They will test in local mode, but I would like them to also do a final test in Hadoop mode.

I would like students to have the option of installing packages for use during map and reduce (e.g., using weathermetrics to convert F to C).  However, it looks like a package needs to be installed on each node.

Has anyone developed a solution for loading R packages on the nodes in the Hadoop cluster?

Cheers  

Rick

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#569] Installing R packages on nodes
parts:
There is an experimental feature to do just that, but it's too unstable and has other drawbacks so we decided to pull it in the next release. The current solution I recommend is: whatever you used to install rmr2 and dependencies, use it. It must work, otherwise we wouldn't have this problem in the first place. If it works for rmr2, Rcpp, digest etc etc. it must work for a variety of packages, if not all. So what is missing, it seems to me, is not a mechanism to install packages on the cluster but a way to make that transparent to the user, make it implicit in a mapreduce call. While that would be nice (the  single machine abstraction is one of the design principles of this package), I don't think that's a show stopper. If it's a policy problem (that is the command to install a package on the cluster exists, but is not available to the students) then whatever we implement in rmr2 will run into the same problem. What am I missing?

Antonio

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#572] Installing R packages on nodes
parts:
Getting the list of packages is the easiest part. The hard part is suppressing the installation procedure output, that ends up in stdout and stdout is reserved for data in hadoop streaming, not messages. There are many ways to control output of commands in R, like capture.output and sink plus others less direct and approved ways, like monkey patching the system call. None worked.


Antonio
